articleTitle: Stability analysis of 2-D systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A polynomial stability criterion for 2-D systems is taken as a starting point for introducing a frequency dependent Lyapunov equation. The Fourier analysis of its matrix solution leads to an infinite dimensional quadratic form which provides a Lyapunov function for the global state of the system. The Fourier coefficients are explicitly obtained as the sum of series involving the system matrices. The convergence of these series constitutes a necessary and sufficient stability condition, which generalizes the analogous condition for 1-D systems.

articleTitle: Improved circuits for the realization of switched-capacitor filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: New topologies for switched-capacitor filters are presented. The circuits are based on a pair of complementary integrators and have transfer functions independent of parasitic capacitances between any node and ground. Design equations are given for low-pass, bandpass, high-pass, and notch biquads, as well as ladder simulation filters. The ladder simulation filters are scaled for optimum dynamic range. Discrete prototypes of both cascade and ladder simulation filters are used to verify the theory.

articleTitle: Block-shift invariance and block implementation of discrete-time filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper describes the general class of linear, time-invariant multivariable systems that can be used in block implementations of time-invariant discrete-time filters. Explicit relations between the properties of the block processor and the properties of the implemented filter are derived, including an explicit expression for the matrix transfer function of the block processor in terms of the single-input, single-output filter transfer function. These properties and relations are independent of the form of realization of the block processor. It is shown that all irreducible state-space realizations of the block processor can be derived by a simple procedure from a simple realization of the required filter transfer function.

articleTitle: Considerations for high-frequency switched-capacitor ladder filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Monolithic filters using switched-capacitor techniques are beginning to be used in commercial audio frequency communication circuits [1], [2], [10]. The fact that these filters are MOS compatible, high precision and low power makes them very attractive in these filter applications. The usefulness of switched-capacitor filters will be greatly increased if the frequency range of these filters can be extended above the voice band. The purpose of this paper is to present the theoretical considerations as well as practical circuits which are useful to the designer attempting to implement high-speed filters.

articleTitle: Exact design of switched-capacitor bandpass filters using coupled-biquad structures
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A method is presented for the design of switched-capacitor bandpass filters using the bilinear<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</tex>-transform. The filters are realized in low-sensitivity coupled-biquad structures and employ biquad circuits which are completely insensitive to stray capacitances between any node and ground. Geometrically symmetric (both all-pole and finite-transmissionzeros) as well as general-parameter filters are treated.

articleTitle: Simplifications and clarifications on the paper 'An algebra of transfer functions for distributed linear time-invariant systems'
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this note we first point out some simplifications in some results of our paper mentioned above [1]. Second, we prove that the algebra of transfer functions<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\hat{\cal B}(\sigma_0)</tex>, introduced in the paper, is in fact the quotient ring of the ring<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\hat{\cal Q}_{_}(\sigma_0)</tex>with respect to the multiplicative system<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\hat{\cal Q}_{_}^{\infty} (\sigma_0)</tex>defined in this note. The analogy between<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\hat{\cal B}(\sigma_0)</tex>, seen as the quotient<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[\hat{\cal Q}_{_}(\sigma_0)][\hat{\cal Q}_{_}^{\infty} (\sigma_0)]^{-1}</tex>, and the algebra of proper rational functions<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C_p (s)</tex>seen as the quotient<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[\Re (\sigma_0)][\Re^{\infty} (\sigma_0)]^{-1}</tex>(where<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\Re_0 (\sigma_0 )</tex>is the ring of proper rational functions analytic in<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Re s \geq \sigma_0</tex>, and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\Re^{\infty} (\sigma_0)</tex>is the multiplicative system of such functions tending to a nonzero constant as<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">|s| \irightarrow \infty</tex>), is fully developed and supports the claim that<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\hat{\cal B} (\sigma_0 )</tex>is a natural extension of the algebra of proper rational functions to distributed systems. These algebraic developments have been found most useful in applications [11], [12].

articleTitle: Finite word effects in block-state realizations of fixed-point digital filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Finite word effects are examined for a class of block realizations that are derived from a state-space realization of the transfer function. For this class of block realizations it is found that the dynamic range of the state variables is independent of block length, roundoff noise decreases with block length and, if the filter is realized in normal form, all autonomous limit cycles can be eliminated.

articleTitle: Passive cascaded lattice digital filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Energy and power analogies are used for the analysis of cascaded (possibly time-varying) lattice digital filters. This approach leads to the requirements for passivity of the sections, and a procedure for the removal of zero-input parasitic oscillations, along with several other results.

articleTitle: Reduction and expansion of live and safe marked graphs
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper it is proved that certain parallel, series, and circuit reductions and expansions on a marked graph do not change the number of its equivalence classes of live and safe markings. The reductions are aseful for the analysis of marked graphs, and the expansions can be used for synthesizing live and safe marked graphs.

articleTitle: An approach to programmable CTD filters using coefficients 0, + 1, and -1
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A delta modulation-like sampled analog filter structure for realizing low-pass filters is described. The filter uses only the coefficients<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0, + 1</tex>, and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</tex>and can be fabricated as a programmable CCD filter. Interpolation and decimation are employed to increase the accuracy of the delta modulation. It is shown that with this scheme a given response can be realized arbitrarily closely. Examples are included.

articleTitle: Transient response of uniformly distributed RLC transmission lines
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the transient response of uniform<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RLC</tex>transmission lines. The case of a general RLC line is examined, along with the special case of a line with low total series resistance. Computer-aided circuit simulations in conjunction with theoretical considerations are used to obtain a physical interpretation of the results. It is shown that for an<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RLC</tex>line terminated In<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R_0 = \sqrt{L/C}</tex>as long as the total series resistance of the line is less than 2.5 R_0, there is no delay penalty caused by pulse distortion on the line. The only delay penalty is caused by the line attenuation, which yields a lower slope for the output waveform.

articleTitle: Switched-capacitor filter design using cascaded sections
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper describes a number of simple (first-, second-, or third-order) switched-capacitor circuits. These can be used as simple self-contained filters, or as filter sections in the cascade realization of a higher order transfer function. All these sections are free from parasitic effects, and all can be designed directly in the sampled-signal domain. Low-pass, high-pass, bandpass, and all-pass circuits are discussed, with and without finite nonzero transmission zeros.

articleTitle: Sign test of multivariable real polynomials
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: New theorems and procedures are presented for testing positivity and nonnegativity of a real polynomial in<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>real variables. The methods pertain to global as well as nonglobal or local sign tests for any closed intervals of the variables. A dimension growth is not required, and the methods depend on resolution of the solution of a set of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>equations in<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>variables. Also provided is a simplified estimation of the computational effort involved in the present procedures, as compared to procedures where a dimension growth is required. Several illustrative examples are also provided.

articleTitle: Switched-capacitor decimation and interpolation circuits
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Novel switched-capacitor decimation and interpolation circuits are described. The decimator can function as an input stage, the interpolator as an output stage in a filter system. This allows the use of differing clock rates in the various stages of the system, which in turn can result in simpler antialiasing requirements, more practical element values and lower sensitivities for the individual filters in the system.

articleTitle: Padé-type order reduction of two-dimensional systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The problem of reducing the order of the transfer function of a given two-dimensional system to a lower order model using Padé-type approximation is considered. Two computational algorithms are proposed. The first is a generalization of the known one-dimensional Padé-type approximation algorithm. The second is a computationally improved version of the first since it involves the parameters of the transfer function of the given system directly, thus circumventing the task of determining the power series expansion coefficients of the given transfer function required in the first algorithm.

articleTitle: The design of arbitrary 2-D zero-phase FIR filters using transformations
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The design of 2-D FIR zero-phase filters by transformations is a popular and well-developed technique, but it suffers from the disadvantage that in its current form only filters with four-quadrant symmetry can be designed. In this contribution a natural generalization is presented which allows the method to be used to design arbitrary zero-phase 2-D FIR filters. This generalization preserves the two most important features of the method-the decoupling of the design problem into one-dimensional and two-dimensional components, and the existence of an efficient structure for realizing the filter.

articleTitle: A Floquet theory of the general linear rotating machine
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: As is well-known, the fundamental assumption underlying Park's decisive analysis of the ideal linear three-phase rotating machine is that all windings on the (nonsalient) stator are in effect sinnsoidally spacially distributed as far as concerns the calculation of any self or mutual magnetic flux linkage. As Park has shown, there exists a suitable reference frame in which such an "ideal" machine admits an internal constant-coefficient differential equation description under the condition of constant rotor angular velocity. On the other hand, if the machine is not Ideal, the various mmf's are no longer sinusoldally distributed and it is not at all obvious that stationarity can be achieved by any choice of frame. Nevertheless, it is shown in this paper that such a "Floquet" frame does Indeed exist and that it may be possible to devise experimental procedures for its determination. This new Park-like theory of the general linear rotating machine subsumes the Ideal case and is based squarely on the obvious geometric periodicity of the machine structure.

articleTitle: A unified approach to optimal recursive digital filter design
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper presents a new optimal recursive digital filter design algorithm to meet simultaneous specifications of magnitude and group delay responses. The technique used is the unconstrained least pth optimization method for a constrained nonlinear programming problem. An illustrative example shows the drastic reduction of group delay ripple in comparison with the all-pass equalizer method.

articleTitle: Multimode oscillations in a coupled oscillator system with fifth-power nonlinear characteristics
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A method for obtaining stability of single and nonresonant double-mode oscillations occurring in a system of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</tex>mutually coupled identical oscillators, is described. These oscillators are characterized by fifth-power nonlinearity. They are coupled by inductances containing resistive components (loss) in a ladder structure. Reduction of stable region of each mode with the increase of the loss is clarified for<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N = 2,3,</tex>and 4 both by the theory and digital simulation.

articleTitle: Optimum design of low-pass switched-capacitor ladder filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A general technique for realizing Bruton's LDI transformation in low-pass switched-capacitor ladder filters is presented, which results is switched-capacitor integrators that are insensitive to parasitic capacitances. It is shown that the correct filter response may be obtained by realizing only the stable poles of the LDI transformed<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">LC</tex>network. Realization of these "stable" poles is reduced to the problem of solving a system of nonlinear equations. The design of a third-order Chebyshev low-pass filter is presented as an example.

articleTitle: Active filters with zero transfer function sensitivity with respect to the time constants of operational amplifiers
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Most second-order RC active filters show a marked dependence on the gain-bandwidth product (GB) of operational amplifiers (OA's) when the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\omega_0</tex>to be realized is greater than 1 percent of GB and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q > 10</tex>. Here designs are given that are virtually independent of OA's when<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\omega_0<0.01</tex>GB and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q < 10</tex>. Even for<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\omega_0=0.05</tex>GB and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q=10</tex>, the center frequency shift due to OA's is less than 0.1 percent. This desirable result is achieved by designing filter amplifiers which have zero first-order sensitivities with respect to the time constant<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\tau = 1/GB</tex>of the OA's used in the design. As a result, the filter transfer function has also zero first-order sensitivity with respect to<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\tau</tex>. General criteria for such designs are given. Experimental results show excellent agreement with theory.

articleTitle: Low-sensitivity switched-capacitor ladder filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A switched-capacitor filter design technique based on the LDI transformation is presented which uses a novel floating inductance simulation circuit. By choosing the filter terminations properly, the circuits are shown to preserve the maximum power transfer property. A low-pass filter design example is presented to illustrate the low-sensitivity property of this technique.

articleTitle: An optimization technique for the design of half-plane 2-D recursive digital filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An iterative optimization technique, based on a Modified Marquardt algorithm, is proposed for the design of asymmetric 2-D half-plane recursive digital filters with a zero-phase implementation. To illustrate the technique a fan-filter and a circular lowpass filter were designed. The technique can also be used for the design of quarter-plane filters.

articleTitle: Stability criteria for off-diagonally monotone nonlinear dynamical systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper discusses the global stability of a nonlinear dynamical system<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\dot{x}=f(x)</tex>in which<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</tex>is a locally Lipschitz continuous off-diagonally monotone function and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f(\theta) > \theta</tex>. Two results are proved: 1) if<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</tex>is piecewise-linear function and if<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-f</tex>is an<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M</tex>-function, then a unique equilibrium point exists and it is globally asymptotically stable; 2) if<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</tex>is a nonlinear function with separate variables in the sense that<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</tex>is given by<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f_{1}(x)= \Sigma^{n}_{j-1}f_{ij}(x_j)</tex>for all<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</tex>, and if<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-f</tex>is an<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M</tex>-function satisfying<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f(x^{\ast})= \theta</tex>for some nonnegative vector<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x^{\ast}</tex>, then<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x^{\ast}</tex>is globally asymptotically stable. These results are applied to the stability analyses of a large scale composite system and a compartmental system.

articleTitle: Noise analysis and comparison of second-order networks containing a single amplifier
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A general noise analysis procedure for single-amplifier feedback systems Is presented and applied to second-order active networks. Noise power spectral density and broad-band noise at the output terminal are calculated using a noise transfer function (NTF). The frequency dependence of the NTF is governed by the poles of the signal transfer functions and is independent of its transmission zeros. It is shown that the noise performance can be optimized by proper design of the passive network. A circuit classification based on the configuration of the feedback network is used for noise comparison and simple formulas applicable to many practical filter applications are presented.

articleTitle: Identification of weakly nonlinear systems using input and output measurements
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new identification technique for a class of weakly nonlinear systems whose behavior is adequately characterized in terms of a finite Volterra functional series is presented. Application of the identification technique results in a complete specification of the nonlinear impulse responses which describe a weakly nonlinear system. The identification technique is a "black box" procedure in that only measurements at the system input and output terminals are required. A functional form for the second-order impulse response,<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h_2(t_1, t_2)</tex>, is derived for a nonlinear system with a finite number of power-law devices. The identification of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h_2(t_1, t_2)</tex>is accomplished by exciting the system with a sum of exponentially decaying signals and appropriately processing the input and output signals using the pencil-of-functions system identification approach. This results in a complete set of linear equations involving all the parameters of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h_2(t_1, t_2)</tex>. Solution of these equations uniquely determines<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h_2(t_l, t_2)</tex>. An example of the practical application of the technique to a common emitter amplifier is presented.

articleTitle: On the topology of FET circuits and the uniqueness of their dc operating points
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: We show here how to prove several results which make it possible to deduce whether or not many common FET circuits can possess more than one, or only one, dc operating point, as a consequence of their topological structure alone. These results extend to FET circuits some similar results which have recently been proved for circuits containing bipolar transistors.

articleTitle: Network transformations
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: From a given 3-terminal linear network realization of a voltage transfer function (VTF)<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</tex>, realizations of five different VTF's expressed in terms of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</tex>are generated without disturbing the internal structure of the original network by employing at the most one additional Ideal operational amplifier. Suitable operators are introduced to express the operations involved in the network transformations. A few applications of these transformations are given.

articleTitle: Theory and recursive computation of 1-D matrix Pade approximants
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Given a matrix power series, it is shown that (except possibly in certain derogatory cases) a recurrence relation relates the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[L+ l/M+1}</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[L/M], [L- l/M- 1]</tex>order Pade approximants, the existence of each of which is guaranteed from validity of a certain rank condition on the corresponding set of characterizing matrices possessing a block-Hankel structure.

articleTitle: Design of actively compensated finite gain amplifiers for high-frequency applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper new circuits for realizing actively compensated finite gain amplifiers (FGA's) using operational amplifiers (OA's) and resistors are given. In IC technology, as the characteristics of the OA's and the resistor ratios track closely with each other with temperature and other variations of ambient conditions, the compensation should hold under such varying conditions. An application is considered in active-RC filters. Experimental results confirm the theoretical predictions. These results show that one can expect a substantial improvement in the operating frequency range of the circuits that employ the new amplifiers over the conventional amplifiers or the existing ones using two OA's.

articleTitle: The elimination of offset errors in dual-slope analog-to-digital converters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new method of eliminating offset error from a dual-slope analog-to-digital converter is described. Two dual-slope cycles, each with the same fixed time period, are needed for a complete conversion. The converter differs from other converters in that the sum and difference of the unknown and reference voltage, as well as the voltages themselves are integrated. Different combinations yield a number of error-free converters in which the ratio of the two voltages is equal to the ratio of the sum or difference of two time periods. The converters also have a limited computational capability In that useful outputs other than the ratio of the unknown and reference voltages can be obtained. For some of the converters the sum or difference of two time periods yields an output with greatly reduced offset error. Another sum or difference provides a correction factor. In addition, some of the converters require a single reference voltage for the entire positive and negative range of the unknown voltage.

articleTitle: Transversal filters with nonuniform tap spacings
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Some basic analytic relationships between tap gains, tap spacings, and sample values of a frequency spectrum on the frequency axis are derived for a transversal filter with nonuniform tap spacings. 'As an application of these results, a few realization conditions are shown for a transversal filter with a definite number of taps, together with several numerical examples.

articleTitle: Parasitic pole approximation techniques for active filter design
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A method of approximating the parasitic poles of active filters employing one, two, or three operational amplifier(s) is presented. These approximations are good for both a single-pole and two-pole model of the operational amplifier and are useful for determining filter stability. The approximation expressions are sufficiently simple that they may be included in the active filter design process. Stability criteria for active filters employing two-pole operational amplifiers are stated in terms of the parasitic pole approximations obtained using the simpler single-pole model of the operational amplifier. The necessity of including the more accurate two-pole model of an operational amplifier in some applications is discussed. Detailed comparisons of the actual and approximate parasitic poles in two examples are made.

articleTitle: Effects of excess phase in multiple-feedback active filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The paper presents theoretical and experimental results showing that lagging "excess phase" of second-order active filter sections causes potentially large errors in the form of a characteristic skewing of the passband shape of multiple-feedback (MF) bandpass functions. It is shown that simple capacitive phase-lead methods eliminate the deviations. The situation is discussed in detail for the specific case of "follow-theleader-feedback" bandpass filters, but applies equally to other MF topologies. Experimental data are presented to demonstrate the effects of excess phase and to verity the correctness of the design process.

articleTitle: Large change response sensitivity of linear networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A general systematic method for determining large-change, multiparameter sensitivity of linear networks is developed from the formal theory of scattering in condensed matter. The method, based on matrix manipulation, constrasts and unifies previous works on analog and digital networks. Standard Basis Operators are introduced as an expedient tool, which aides in the solution of scattering matrix equations. Explicit exact sensitivity formulas are developed for several types of multiparameter changes in both analog and digital networks.

articleTitle: On the stability and well-posedness of interconnected nonlinear dynamical systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems

articleTitle: Inductively tuned astable multivibrator
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The operation of an inductively tuned astable multivibrator of basic form is analyzed. Characteristic equations, essential waveforms, and a negative resistance interpretation are presented. Certain applications are suggested.

articleTitle: A note on the 2-D partial fraction expansion
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this note it is shown that the 2-D composition<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\frac{A(z_1,z_2)A(z_{1}^{-1},z_{2}^{-1})} {B(z_1,z_2)B(z_{1}^{-1},z_{2}^{-1})} =</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\frac{P(z_1,z_2)}{B(z_1,z_2)} + \frac{P(z_{1}^{-1},z_{2}^{-1})}{B(z_{1}^{-1},z_{2}^{-1})}</tex>contrary to the 1-D case, does not exist in general. Conditions for the existence of such a decomposition are obtained and applied to two examples.

articleTitle: Switched-capacitor transconductance and related building blocks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new element, the switched-capacitor transconductance, is developed and used to construct several other active switched-capacitor building blocks: amplifiers with gain defined by the ratio of capacitors, integrators, inductors, and gyrators. The element is also used to design a switched-capacitor biquad. All reported networks were fabricated with discrete components and tested. Experimental data for the biquad are given.

articleTitle: Multiple-pole-and-zero approximation of general attenuation specifications
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new approximation method is proposed to realize transfer functions in which the multiplicity of each real pole (zero)- and complex pole (zero)-pair may be imposed by the designer. These functions may be evaluated to satisfy any assigned attenuation specification, and, hence, allow the design of filters by cascading low-order blocks with lower<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>-factors, compared with the usual simple-pole solutions. This result is very practicable in the construction of highly selective<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RC</tex>-active filters. A complete algorithm is implemented to evaluate these functions.

articleTitle: Analysis of active RC networks by decomposition
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A method is developed for rapid and intuitive analysis of active<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RC</tex>networks. Only first-order time constants or poles and resistive voltage transfer ratios need be computed, these being calculated with the various capacitors replaced by either shorts- or open-circuits. A computation graph is presented for ordering the calculations.

articleTitle: Injection locked tunable filters and amplifiers
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The problem of realizing coherent filters and amplifiers using injection-lock technique has been discussed in this short communication. It deals with the behavior of an injection synchronized oscillator (ISO) under different situations: i) it evaluates the locking range of an ISO in response to an FM signal corrupted with an additive random noise, ii) it finds the coherent filtering capability, and iii) it discusses its amplifying property. The experimental results have been presented in support of the theoretical approach.

articleTitle: ROM/ACC realization of digital filters for poles near the unit circle
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Two all-pole filter structures proposed by Agarwal and Burrus have small roundoff error and coefficient sensitivity for poles near the unit circle. Assuming equal word lengths for input and output, we first give expressions for the mean-squared noise-to-signal<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(N/S)</tex>ratios in these structures. We then consider implementation of the Agarwal-Burrus structures using multiplierless ROM-accumulator (ROM/ACC) arithmetic. The<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N/S</tex>ratios, including sensitivity considerations, are presented and shown to be small. In addition, limit cycle bounds are given and also shown to be small. An example demonstrates that the new realixations may require as little as one-half the ROM word length and operate at up to twice the word rate of direct form ROM/ACC realizations that achieve the same<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S/N</tex>.

articleTitle: A note on the application of FFT to the solution of a system of Toeplitz normal equations
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: This note presents an approach to the solution of a system of Toeplitz normal equations, based on using iterative techniques, the circulant matrices and the fast Fourier transform algorithm. The number of computations required and the roundoff errors associated with this method are discussed. The merits and demerits of this approach are compared with the Trench's algorithm.

articleTitle: Elimination of granularity and overflow limit cycles in minimum norm recursive digital filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A method of guaranteeing asymptotic stability in a recursive digital filter (using fixed point arithmetic) is presented. Using this method a particular implementation of the second-order "coupled form" recursive digital filter is demonstrated to be completely free from limit cycle oscillations under zero input conditions.

articleTitle: A different look at roundoff noise in digital filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: One of the sources of inaccuracy due to finite word length Implementation of digital filters is the multiplication roundoff noise. In this paper, two new approaches are outlined and illustrated for the calculation of this noise, by using digital all-pass functions as the basis. Both of these methods are shown to have computational advantages over the conventional ones.

articleTitle: On the Periodic Steady-State Problem by the Newton Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The methods by which linear sensitivity circuits have been used to evaluate the sensitivity matrix,<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">{\partial}x(T)/{\partial}x(0)</tex>, can be improved. The sensitivity matrix is used in the computation of the Jacobian of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f(x(0))=x(0)-x(T)=0</tex>, (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</tex>being the period) in a periodic steady-state problem. It is shown here that the sensitivity matrix can be obtained from the solution of a linear homogeneous matrix equation which is simply derived by differentiating the state equations or a mixture of algebraicdifferential equations arising from any formulation. This simplification makes the method easier and more practical to implement in a general purpose CAD program. Examples are given.

articleTitle: Switched-capacitor filters using FDNR-like super capacitances
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Switched-capacitor networks have become very attractive for the MOS/LSI realization of analog sampled-data filters. The work presented in this paper shows that the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l/p</tex>transformation where<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p =(1 -z^{-2})/ {\tau}</tex>can be performed for such filters similarly to Bruton's<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/s</tex>transformation for analog continuous networks. An analog sampled-data filter based on this principle has been designed and implemented using discrete components.

articleTitle: Variable digital filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: IIR prototype filters cannot be used for the design of variable filters through Schüssler's all-pass transformation because of the occurrence of delay-free loops; no such problem arises with FIR prototypes. In this paper, the drawbacks of the latter type, with regard to computational efficiency and output roundoff noise, have been brought out, An approach is suggested, wherein the delay-free loops with IIR prototypes are eliminated by modifying the coefficients of the first- and second-order sections of the prototype filter. The computation of modified coefficients In this approach requires fewer multiplications as compared to an existing method.

articleTitle: Stability domains for second-order recursive digital filters in normal form with 'matrix power' feedback
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The allowable pole locations that will provide guaranteed immunity from finite-word limit cycles are derived for a class of secondorder normal digital filters.

articleTitle: Unsolved theoretical problem in design of optimal low-pass filter for harmonic suppression in radio-transmitter output
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The author offers to cooperate in development of an optimal harmonic-suppression output filter for power amplifiers. The commonly used elliptic-function filter is not optimal for this purpose: less attenuation is needed at higher frequencies in the stopband. An improved design should provide a value of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A_{\min}</tex>that varies with frequency as the harmonic output of the amplifier varies with frequency.

articleTitle: Active complementary networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Complementary networks are defined. A condition for a multi-port active network to yield complementary networks is derived. Some new filters are derived employing complementary network transformation.

articleTitle: Nullor equivalent networks of nonideal operational amplifiers and voltage-controlled sources
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Equivalent networks of the operational amplifier with finite gain-bandwidth (a VCVS) are given. These equivalent networks consist of resistors, capacitors, and nuillator-norator pairs. Equivalent networks are shown for the basic operational amplifier feedback connections (i.e., inverting, noninverting, and differential). The networks are extended to include the other principal deviations from the ideal operational amplifier. The technique of applying the new models to the generation of improved active networks is then described.

articleTitle: Effect of correlation between transactions errors on fixed-point fast Fourier transform analysis
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A revised expression, taking the effect of correlation between truncation errors, is obtained for the output noise-to-signal when the fast Fourier transform (FFT) is computed in fixed-point arithmetic. The results are given for the two common forms of the FFT algorithmn, decimation in-frequency and in-time. The analysis assumes sign-magnitude (or 1's complement) arithmetic and is presented in detail for the decimation-in-frequency (DIF) case. The correlation coefficients are computed analytically. A few assumptions, made in the analysis, are verified by computer simulations. The average variance of the output noise, due to the truncation errors, predicted by the new model is approximately twice the corresponding value predicted by the old model (which assumes that the truncation errors are uncorrelated). The output noise-to-signal ratios predicted by the revised and old expressions are compared with experimental results. It is shown that the revised result predicts much closer to the experimental results than the old.

articleTitle: Temporal stability of N-dimensional linear processors and its applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The transfer function of an<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</tex>-dimensional linear processor is the double-ended<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\overrightarrow{z}</tex>-transform of its impulse response function. Every rational transfer function has a unique, stable expansion if the denominator polynomial is nonzero on the unit circle product subspace of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\overrightarrow{z}</tex>, and can be realized by a frame recursive processing scheme. As an extension of the above the present paper stated and proved the conditions for an active infinite network to be stable both spatially and temporally.

articleTitle: The Klee and Quaife minimum (d, 1, 3)-graphs revisited
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: After Klee and Qualfe [1], a<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(d,c,\upsilon)</tex>-graph<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</tex>is one which is regular of degree<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\upsilon</tex>, diameter<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</tex>, and connectivity<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</tex>, so that<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</tex>is necessarily at most v; and G is said to be minimum if it is of minimum order. The cited authors have noted that such a graph is that of a survivable communication network in which the lines of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</tex>represent the communication channels, its points representing the switching centers (stations) at which messages originate or are received, or through which they are routed. The network remains connected when fewer than c stations (and hence certainly fewer than<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</tex>channels) are incapacitated. They exhibited and classified all minimuim<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(d, 1, 3)</tex>-graphs and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(d, 2,3)</tex>-graphs, i.e., all minimum cubic graphs of diameter<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</tex>and connectivity<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c \leq 2</tex>, and gave counts of their numbers. The purpose of the present paper is expository: we derive Klee and Qualfe's aesthetic and complete results by a different technique which provides new insights into the general<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(d, c,\upsilon)</tex>-graph problem through the use of associated pseudographs to generate nonseparable minimum blocks. We also introduce and use the new concepts of bridge trees and of a cut-diameter graph. We differ from Klee and Qualfe in defining a graph<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</tex>to be<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</tex>-connected if and only if removal of some minimum set of c of its points disconnects<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</tex>, whereas they considered such a graph to be k-connected for all nonzero values of k less than or equal to c, when<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c > 0</tex>. And except where otherwise defined, our terminology is Harary's [2].

articleTitle: Eigenvalue-S matrix element relations for some common devices with two-fold symmetry using group theory
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Linear relations between the S matrix eigenvalues and S matrix entries of symmetrical multi-port networks have frequently been useful for understanding the properties of such networks. Generally, they have only been derived for networks possessing sufficient symmetry to allow the application of methods based on matrix algebra. Some common multi-port devices possess only two-fold symmetry, however. In this paper a technique based on group theory is developed for systematically deriving such relations in cases of limited symmetry as well.

articleTitle: Unified single-amplifier filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A unified treatment of single-amplifer filters is described using a linear-graph representation of the passive<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RC</tex>section. This allows identification of familiar active networks in terms of branch admittances and the incorporation of amplifier Imperfections.

articleTitle: Design of sharp cutoff low-pass maximally flat RC-active filters by cascading third-order blocks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Pairs of coincident<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j{\omega}</tex>-axis zeros are added to the multiple real root maximally flat (MURROMAF) approximation function for designing sharp cutoff low-pass<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RC</tex>-active filters. Expressions for transfer function and cutoff slope are derived in terms of the order<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</tex>, the multiplicity of the real pole<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\mu</tex>, the number of pairs of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j{\omega}</tex>-axis zeros<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</tex>and their locations. A design example is also given to illustrate the procedure for finding out the best transfer function.

articleTitle: Computational technique for the periodic steady-state analysis of large nonlinear circuits
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A comparison of the computation speed and storage requirements of three algorithms for the determination of the periodic steadystate response of nonlinear circulits, namely the Newton, extrapolation, and gradient methods, shows the latter to be the most attractive if an efficient function minimization routine is available. The gradient algorithm equations have been derived on the basis of a general tableau representation of the network equations which, in contrast to the recently reported state variable formulation, lends itself to straightforward implementation in modern, network, transient analysis programs which use sparse matrix techniques. The algorithm has been implemented with one such program and tested on several circuits using two optimization routines. Satifactory results are obtained with the variable metric routine but convergence is sensitive to scaling and the initial time.

articleTitle: On the suppression of zero-input parasitic oscillations in floating point wave digital filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Fettweis [1] has given a condition which guarantees, if satisfied, the absence of zero-input parasitic oscillations in wave digital filters. In this paper a method is given which can be used to implement this condition in the case of floating point arithmetic.

articleTitle: Addendum to 'Limit cycles in state-space structures for digital filters'
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems

articleTitle: A switched-capacitor high-pass filter
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A high-pass switched-capacitor biquadratic filter section is described. It is economical and has sufficiently low sensitivities to element-value variations and parasitics to make it useful in a variety of applications. For analog input, it can be supplemented with a first-order filter section which prevents direct signal leakthrough.

articleTitle: Maximally flat magnitude circularly symmetric two-dimensional low-pass IIR digital filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A straightforward method is proposed to design a class of causal, two-dimensional, infinite impulse response digital filters which possess circularly symmetric, maximally flat magnitude, low-pass responses. This class of filters has the characteristic that the numerator and the denominator of the corresponding digital transfer function individually possess approximately circularly symmetric magnitude responses. Under this condition, the proposed method requires the design of a one-dimensional transfer function satisfying the frequency selective properties and a simple modification which transforms the one-dimensional function into a circularly symmetric two-dimensional function. Low-pass filters with maximally flat magnitude are obtained and the characteristics of the resulting functions indicate that they possess good circular symmetry.

articleTitle: An efficient design of large-scale communication networks with a decomposition technique
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper presents an efficient network design method that can be used for large-scale communication networks employing both satellite and terrestrial links. The basic design problem is outlined along with mathematical models. Then a Lagrangian multiplier is used to decompose the design problem of a large-scale multinode network into that of a "coupled" set of three-node networks. This decomposition technique greatly simplifies the network design and enhances the computational efficiency. A 30-node network example is shown for illustration.

articleTitle: On the inadequacies of loop gain in broad-band, multiloop feedback amplifiers
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Experience in communications engineering has repeatedly shown that loop gain can be an unreliable basis for the assessment of stability margins in feedback amplifiers. There are both theoretical and practical reasons for this. A simple identity provides a sounder theoretical basis, and provides a novel way of looking at old problems. The presence of any unstable modes of the closed-loop amplifier can be predicted with more assurance from open-loop measurements by examining a product of functions derived from the identity rather than a single-loop gain. Further improvements in stability assessment are possible by using the data base of the embedding network method [1]. The loop gains computed from the data base can be compared with those derived directly from two-port s-parameter measurements at the corresponding nodes, thus avoiding the use of circuit diagrams. Results on several practical amplifiers are quoted, which show that plots of loop gains can fail to predict closed-loop instability. In another actual case, a loop gain failed to predict conditional stability. The correct predictions in each case were obtained using the method described in [1].

articleTitle: Frequency dependence of sensitivities in second-order RC active filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper presents that gain and phase sensitivities to some element in biquadratic filters approximately constitute a circle on the complex sensitivity plane, provided that the quality factor<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>of the circuit is appreciably larger than unity. Moreover, the group delay sensitivity is represented by the imaginary part of a cardioid. Using these results, we obtain bounds of maximum values of gain, phase, and group delay sensitivities. Further, it is proved that the maximum values of these sensitivities can be simultaneously minimized by minimizing the absolute value of the transfer function sensitivity at the center frequency provided that<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\omega_0</tex>-sensitivities are constant and do not contain design parameters. Next, a statistical variability measure for the optimal-rdter design is proposed. Finally, the relation between some variability measures proposed uptil now is made clear.

articleTitle: A generalized algorithm for the inversion of Cauer type continued fractions
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new generalized algorithm, which can be programmed on a digital computer, is established for performing the inversion of the Cauer type continued fractions.

articleTitle: High speed current mode logic for LSI
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A high speed/low power logic family is described which combines the best features of current mode logic (CML), emitter-coupled logic (ECL), and emitter function logic (EFL). This is combined with a low voltage-current source, using the principle of current imaging, to provide three levels of series gating with reduced supply voltages. With relatively slow transistors (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f_1</tex>=500 MHz) circuit structures have been fabricated which provide several logic levels with a total delay of 2<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ns</tex>and total power dissipation of 2 mW per circuit structure. The paper also describes the implementation of ROM's, RAM's, and PLA's using the principle of current steering. An analysis is given for circuit operation with variation in supply voltage and temperature. Three fabricated LSI chips are described with an average of 1000 equivalent gates per chip.

articleTitle: A radial exploration algorithm for the statistical analysis of linear circuits
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: This communication presents a new approach to the statistical analysis of linear circuits. The method is based on a two-stage sampling scheme in which random directions are first generated in multiparameter component space, and then sample points are selected in each direction, the points being generated according to a modified probability density function within the tolerance region. An efficient tracking-sensitivity algorithm based on a matrix series expansion is utilized to approximate the circuit response values at the sample points. A technique for reducing the variance associated with the yield estimate is also discussed. The results are compared with those obtained by conventional Monte Carlo methods for a test example. Considerable savings in computational effort have been observed.

articleTitle: A new class of RC-active filters using FDNR-elements and generalized terminations
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The synthesis of a new class of RC-active filters that uses FDNR-elements and generalized terminations is described. The various possibilities are exhibited in general and for an example the method is carried through.

articleTitle: Stability analysis of two-dimensional digital recursive filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new approach to the stability problem for the two-dimensional digital recursive filter is presented. The bivariate difference equation representation of the two-dimensional recursive digital filter Is converted to a multiinput-muliloutput (MIMO) system similar to the statespace representation of the one-dimensional digital recursive filter. In this paper, a pseudo-state representation is used and three coefficient matrices are obtained. A general theorem for stability of two-dimensional digital recursive filters is derived and a very useful theorem is presented which expresses sufficient requirements for instability in terms of the spectral radii of these matrices.

articleTitle: On the dynamic range of wave digital filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Dynamic range performance is studied for a group of two-port wave digital filters, all of which satisfy the same attenuation specifications. Two dual prototype networks are used as well as four different sampling frequencies. The design is a 12th-order bandpass filter with high performance requirements.

articleTitle: Locking characteristics of synchronized oscillators in presence of interference
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: This correspondence begins with a critical review of the phenomenon of injection synchronization in an oscillator incorporating a low-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>tank circuit. A technique of improving the locking time of an injection synchronized oscillator (ISO) has been suggested. Also presented is a method of evaluating the locking range and locking time of an ISO in the presence of an interfering tone. The response of an ISO to an FM signal has been studied. Experimental results corroborating the theoretical findings have been given.

articleTitle: Passive realization of a class of time-varying networks having a compatible transform
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Necessary and sufficient conditions for the realization of a class of passive time-varying networks having a compatible transform are derived.

articleTitle: Optimum addition of an edge to a path
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Let<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q(G)</tex>denote the sum taken over all vertex pairs<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u,v</tex>of a graph<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</tex>of the shortest distance from<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</tex>to<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</tex>in<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</tex>. We determine the edges e which when added to the path<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P_m</tex>minimize<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q(P_{m} + e)</tex>. For example, if<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1,{\cdots},2n+ 1</tex>is the vertex sequence of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P_{2n +1}</tex>, the unique optimum edge is<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e=[a, 2n+2-a]</tex>, where<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a = [n(\sqrt{2} - 1)]</tex>.

articleTitle: Spectral analysis of switched-capacitor filters designed using the bilinear z-transform
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Analytic formulas are derived for the frequency response of switched-capacitor filters containing periodically reversed capacitors. The contribution of signal leakthrough is analyzed, and its elimination using Impulse sampling or a sample-and-hold circuit discussed. The effect of a time displacement between switching and sampling Is also derived. Computed and measured responses of a fifth-degree filter are given.

articleTitle: Passive element sensitivity of second-order RC active filter sections
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A general method is used to evaluate the passive element sensitivity performance of second order LP and BP filter sections, and to compare some well-known circuit types. In particular it is shown that simple single-amplifier networks can be less sensitive than analog computer types. These conclusions are verified by a Monte Carlo simulation.

articleTitle: A canonical form for a state-space model in two-dimensional systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A canonical form is presented for a dass of Roesser's model such that the denominator of the transfer function can be expressed by product of two polynomials with a variable, where the model is assumed to be separately locally controllable or observable. This form will be obtained by extending a well-known canonical form in one-dimensional linear systems to two-dimensional case.

articleTitle: Ladder wave digital filters realizing complex attenuation poles
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: It is known that for wave digital filters (WDF) either their transmittance or their reflectance can be used as transfer function. So far, only the first possibility has been examined in detail. However, if a WDF is derived from a reference ladder network composed of inductances, capacitances, and/or unity elements, complex attenuation poles (transmission zeros) cannot then be obtained. It is shown in this paper that one can design a ladder WDF using the reflectance in order to obtain attenuation poles at complex frequencies. The sensitivity characteristics of a filter designed in this way are also presented.

articleTitle: Theory, design, and applications of D-T linear transformation circuits
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new class of circuits which allows a prescribed driving point characteristic to be obtained by a linear transformation on a transfer characteristic is defined. The usefulness of these circuits and their application to the synthesis of resistive nonlinear networks is discussed. Also experimental data on their performance are given. Finally, a formal treatment is given which allows the definition of a multidimensional linear transformation converters (LTC).

articleTitle: Existence and uniqueness results for Liénard́s equation having a dead band
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: In the first part of the present paper we consider general systems of first-order autonomous differential equations and generalize a uniqueness criterion by Dulac concerning periodic solutions to equations of the form<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\dot{x}=P(x,y), \dot{y}=Q(x,y)</tex>. In the second part we use this result to generalize a uniqueness theorem by de Figueiredo concerning periodic solutions to Liénard's equation<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\ddot{x} +f(x)\dot{x} + g(x) = 0</tex>. By our method we are able to avoid the hitherto usual condition<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">xg(x) > 0, x {\neq} 0</tex>, which excludes the possibility for the equation to have a dead band. Finally, we prove an existence theorem concerning periodic solutions to such equations. The use of the theorems is illustrated by a simple example in the last section.

articleTitle: The product matrices and new gain formulas
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: New matrices, the product matrix<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P</tex>, the voltage product matrix<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p^{\upsilon}</tex>, and the current product matrix<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P^i</tex>, are defined at first. And new gain formulas<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T^{\upsilon}_{qp}</tex>for the voltage gain and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T^{i}_{qp}</tex>, for the current gain are presented on the basis of the product matrices. Although the formulas are topological ones, the procedures for their evaluations are quite systematic, completely indirect and purely numerical, and no sign rule is required. So the new formulas are suitable for computer-aided symbolic network analysis without restriction on symbols, in number or type.

articleTitle: Analysis and design of tracking filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper presents a study of tracking filters. Such filters are industrially important and useful in those applications requiring tight bandwidth control for obtaining improved signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). A "high-Q" tracking filter achieves good SNR and will "track" a wandering carrier frequency to maintain the same SNR. This paper outlines the analysis and design of tracking filters. The filter transfer function<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H_{TF}(s)</tex>and model will be presented. The transient responses will be predicted using the filter transfer function. Design procedures will also be outlined. These procedures will be used to design a typical tracking filter.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Active RC Systems with a Multiport Gyrator and Defined Structure
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A generalized analytical method is suggested for the theoretical synthesis of active<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RC</tex>systems with a multiport gyrator. The method is based on the analysis of an idealized nullor structure of a multiport gyrator given in a previous work. The method consists in setting up a theoretical model of the system under analysis by means of a matrix whose elements are voltage transfer functions. The parameters of the passive RC multiport elements and the gyrator are determined in order to achieve the transfer functions. The real parameters of the gyrator are determined by replacing each nullor by a real operational amplifier. The validity of the method is verified on an example.

articleTitle: Iterative procedures for solution of nonlinear electrical networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The linearization of nonlinear electrical elements by means of tangent is commonly applied in solving nonlinear electrical networks. Here the linearization is discussed by means of secant (in regula falsi mode) and it is compared with the tangent method. It is shown that by combining the positive properties of both the secant and tangent methods, it is possible to ensure convergence even in case the tangent method alone has been inefficient.

articleTitle: On single-row routing
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new lower limit on the street congestion in single-row routing is presented.

articleTitle: High-Q inductance circuit using an integrator and its application
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper we propose a high-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>inductance simulation circuit using an integrator and a voltage-current converter. This is followed by a description of an application of this circuit to realize a high-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>bandpass amplifier. The input voltage<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">E_i</tex>, is integrated and the resulting output<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">E_0</tex>is converted to a current<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">I_i</tex>whose magnitude and phase are proportional to those of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">E_0</tex>. So the phase angle of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">I_0</tex>lags<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">E_i</tex>by almost 90 degs. The design of the integrator circuit which provides a phase lag of 90 degs is described; analysis of the effect of element tolerances and temperature variations, frequency range over which the effective inductance has nearly constant value, and the maximum value of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>attainable by adjusting the circuit parameters are presented. It is also shown that over a frequency range of about 1 Hz-500 kHz, maximum values of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>in the range of 500-1500 may be realized stably. Finally, a frequency selective amplifier using an inductance circuit with an unloaded<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>of 830 is described to illustrate the stability of such high-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>circuits.

articleTitle: The method for determination small-signal admittance matrix of the RC transmission line with voltage-controlled parameters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new recursive method for determination of the small-signal admittance matrix of the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RC</tex>transmission line with voltage-controlled parameters is proposed. This method is based on the solution of the resulting Fredholm integral equation and is valid for the lines described by the homogeneous and nonhomogeneous differential equations.

articleTitle: Equivalent circuits for switched-capacitor networks including recharging devices
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Equivalent circuits for switched-capacitor (SC) networks including recharging devices are derived. Parasitic effects, like stray capacitances and nonideal op amps, are taken into account. As a result, the equivalent time-invariant network is split up into a frequency dependent impedance network and a purely (negative) resistive network which corresponds directly to the capacitor network of the SC-filter and allows for the loss compensation achieved by the recharging switching devices. In general, these two parts of the equivalent network are coupled via generalized impedance converters (GIC's).

articleTitle: An active circuit for elliptic-type filters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An active filter circuit is presented that realizes second-order stages of band-reject fiters of all types, and low-pass, high-pass, and bandpass filters of elliptic and inverse Chebyshev types. The circuit is comparable in complexity (having either one more or one less resistor depending on the mode of operation of one op amp) and in sensitivities to the popular biquad circuits that realize all-pole low-pass prototype filters.

articleTitle: On the design of broad-band 90° phase-splitting networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A new design method is developed for 90 ° phase-splitting networks which have arbitrary single-sideband suppression characteristic. The proposed method is based on the insertion loss filter design approach. Characteristic function of a 90 ° phase-splitting network is defined, and Its properties are investigated. The investigation leads to the development of a design procedure by which a computer program can be readily used with minor modification of subprograms in an automatic filter synthesis procedure. Several examples show versatility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A note on the representation and realization of lumped-distributed networks, delay-differential systems, and 2-D systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: It is apparent from existing results that the realization of lumped-distributed networks, delay-differential systems, and two-dimensional (2-D) systems is similar in some respects. But there are also several important differences which have received little or no attention in the literature. In this note, similarities and differences in the theory of these three types of network-systems are discussed.

articleTitle: An approximation of a transfer function by one with lower Q's
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: This article presents a method for interchanging a portion of a transfer function with high<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>-factor poles by a more complicated transfer function that can be realized with lower<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>-factor stages. The limit for the possible<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>-factor lowering is determined by the root locus for the poles of this high<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>-portion. The approximation error can be reduced in a geometric progression by increasing the number of low<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Q</tex>-factor stages. A method for determining the poles and zeros of the approximating function is described and an example of interchange of a bandpass filter transfer function is given.

articleTitle: A note on parameter value determination from node voltage measurements
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
abstract: In a recent paper a method was presented for the calculation of element value changes from node voltage changes. The method was derived using Tellegen's conservation of power theorem. In this short note it is shown that an equivalent result can be obtained by applying Kirchhoff's current law to a cutset.

articleTitle: NewL_2-instability criteria for large-scale interconnected systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems
